title: Exploiting Human Color Discrimination for Memory- and Energy-Efficient Image Encoding in Virtual Reality
problem: DRAM access energy is a significant portion of VR system energy, and existing framebuffer compression uses numerically lossless algorithms that do not exploit human perceptual limitations.
motivation: Virtual Reality requires efficient computing substrates to become ubiquitous, making DRAM traffic optimization critical for system energy reduction.
method: The algorithm leverages psychophysical studies showing humans cannot discriminate perceptually close colors, especially in peripheral vision. It adjusts pixel colors to minimize bit encoding cost while maintaining visual quality. Lightweight architectural support enables real-time compression in the framebuffer pipeline.
key_novelty: Exploiting human color discrimination limitations in both central and peripheral vision to enable perceptually-lossless but numerically-lossy compression.
contributions: Algorithm that adjusts pixel colors based on human color discrimination ability to minimize encoding cost
Lightweight architectural support for real-time framebuffer compression
Achieves 66.9% DRAM traffic reduction with 20.4% improvement over existing framebuffer compression
Validation through psychophysical studies on human participants

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 66.9% DRAM traffic reduction, 20.4% improvement over baseline
metrics.accuracy: Minimal perceptual fidelity degradation validated through psychophysical studies

limitations: Specific limitations of the approach are not discussed in the abstract.
